summary: Intermittent packet loss to internal k8s API when on guest VLAN + NAT hairpin; VPN connected but services unreachable
description:
Issue summary:
Users on corporate guest Wi-Fi intermittently report that the VPN client connects successfully but internal services (k8s API, internal build agents) are unreachable or show high packet loss. This started after an AP config roll last night that adjusted guest VLAN isolation and NAT behavior.

Impact:
Multiple engineers across the us-east office cannot push builds or access cluster APIs from laptops when connected to guest SSID and with VPN running. Ticket escalated to Network + Endpoint.

Environment:
- Wi-Fi: corporate-guest (802.11ax, AP firmware 3.14.7)
- VPN agent: RedwoodZeroTrust v1.8.3 (auto-update enabled)
- Edge NAT: Branch NAT gateway (version 6.2.1) with hairpinning enabled for host policies
- Affected clients: MacBook Pro (macOS 14.2), Windows 11 laptops
- Time window: 2026-03-10 02:00–ongoing (local office timezone)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect to corporate-guest SSID at us-east office.
2) Start RedwoodZeroTrust VPN and confirm connection to corp network.
3) Attempt kubectl get pods against internal k8s API (api.internal.redwood).
4) Observe intermittent packet loss, TCP retransmits, or connection resets.

Observed behavior:
- VPN status shows "Connected" and internal routes are pushed.
- tcpdump on client shows SYN retransmits and occasional RSTs returned from gateway IP instead of k8s API.
- Some flows complete after multiple retries; others consistently fail.
- When the same client uses wired office network or different SSID (employee-ssid), behavior is normal.

Expected behavior:
- VPN should route traffic to internal services without packet loss or asymmetric resets regardless of Wi-Fi SSID.

Initial hypothesis:
- NAT hairpinning + client isolation on guest VLAN may be causing asymmetric return path or incorrect session translation on the edge NAT.
- AP roaming/power-save could interact with NAT session timeouts, causing transient state that returns RSTs.
- Possible broken conntrack entries or aggressive TCP reset policy on the edge device for hairpinned traffic.
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:15 - Collected tcpdump from affected MacBook: saw SYN->...->SYN-ACK path: client->vpn-tunnel->edge-nat, but retransmits when return path translated to guest-gateway IP with port rewrite.

03/10 09:42 - Captured NAT table snapshot from edge gateway (snipped): many short-lived nat entries for hairpin flows with inconsistent timeout values. Observed entries where src translated twice (SNAT then DNAT).

03/10 10:05 - Reproduced locally: when AP client isolation enabled, hairpinned flows show average RTT spikes and occasional TCP RST coming from NAT device rather than internal service IP, indicating asymmetric translation or firewall aborts.
03/10 11:30 - Confirmed that on employee-ssid (no guest VLAN isolation, same AP), flows succeed. Isolating the guest VLAN configuration change last night correlates with incident start time.
03/10 12:00 - Endpoint logs (RedwoodZeroTrust) show no authentication or tunnel errors; keepalive and routes are stable. So problem is likely in infra path after the tunnel egress.

03/10 13:20 - packet capture from branch NAT to k8s API shows return packets' source IP being rewritten to branch-gateway IP with expected source port, but client sees different 4-tuple, causing conntrack mismatch on clientside NAT stack -> RST.
03/10 14:05 - Cross-referenced with firewall rules: a new rule added in change CHG-2026-0310-guest-nat modified 'hairpin-reflect' to use dynamic port mapping; rollback recommended for testing.
03/10 15:40 - Slack thread: #net-ops: https://slack.redwood/archives/C02NETOPS/p167890 - included initial packet captures and NAT table screenshots.
comments: Aria Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10 09:20: I can repro consistently on two machines. Attaching tcpdump in shared drive. Please advise if I should try toggling AP config.

Marcus Nguyen (Network) 2026-03-10 09:50: I've pulled NAT logs; looks like hairpin translation rules were tightened in last night's change. Will try temporary rule revert in staging before touching prod.

SRE (Jordan Lee) 2026-03-10 11:10: From cluster side, no ingress throttles or errors. k8s API receiving packets but connection resets appear upstream. Recommend NAT rollback/testing as Marcus suggested.
Marcus Nguyen 2026-03-10 14:30: Rolled back CHG-2026-0310-guest-nat in trial VLAN. Reproduced scenario: trial VLAN shows no packet loss. Scheduling prod rollback window at 16:00 if no objections.

Network Ops (Priya Shah) 2026-03-10 15:00: Raising caution: full rollback could expose guest-to-guest traffic; temporary mitigation will be to disable dynamic port mapping for hairpin only for VPN-sourced subnets.
Aria Patel 2026-03-12 08:45: After partial rollback/mapping change, engineers report improved stability. Marking as in progress while we monitor.
resolution_notes: Workaround (applied 2026-03-10 16:10): Reverted CHG-2026-0310-guest-nat dynamic hairpin port mapping for vpn-source subnets. This removed double translation and reduced RSTs. Noted in change log.

Permanent fix plan: Network to implement explicit hairpin reflexive rule with consistent conntrack timeouts for guest VLAN and exclude VPN-terminating ranges from guest isolation rewriting. Owner: Marcus Nguyen. ETA: 2026-03-19.

Follow-ups: add automated packet-capture regression test when AP/profile changes are rolled out; add a confluence page documenting hairpin interaction with zero-trust VPNs. Added playbook to net-ops runbook.
Status: Partial mitigation applied; monitoring in prod for 72 hours. If stable, close ticket and schedule permanent config change during maintenance window.
